cards.stock: fossil-fuelled electricity generation in the grids Orsted supplies (host stock: atmospheric CO2, 425 ppm against the 350 ppm boundary)
cards.evidence: Orsted power generation 38.4 TWh in 2024, +8% on 2023, 97% renewable (Annual Report 2024, reported by Enerdata); offshore generation +6% in 2025 on 10.2 GW installed offshore capacity with 8.1 GW under construction (Annual Report 2025, 6 Feb 2026); UK fossil-fuelled generation 93.1 TWh in 2025 against 131.6 TWh in 2021 (42.6% of 309 TWh) while renewables reached 152.5 TWh and 52.5% share (DESNZ Energy Trends, 2025 data) [class 3, agency series applied to disclosed volume]
cards.note: Gate fail on dilution: 900,816,600 new shares issued at DKK 66.60 on 420,381,080 existing shares, rights issue completed 6 Oct 2025 raising DKK 59.56bn at 99.3% subscription, share count +214% inside three years. B 17 and not higher: revenue of DKK 73.2bn in 2025 includes power trading and the Hornsea 3 transmission asset sale, and 3% of 2024 generation was non-renewable; class 3 caps B at 20. C1 7: electricity demand is set by the system, no enlarging statement located. C2 7: a decarbonised grid is the product. D_rep 2: growth by enlargement of single bespoke projects, and Hornsea 4 (2,400 MW) was discontinued in May 2025 at break-away costs of DKK 3.5-4.5bn. D_inhib 1: DKK 60bn of fresh equity plus the 2025-26 divestment programme (50% of Hornsea 3, 55% of Greater Changhua 2, European onshore) were required to fund the committed build, dividend suspended FY2023-2025. F_clock 3 on the asset basis: Orsted owns the generating stock and the Layer 0 ghg clock is 20 to 40 years of energy capital turnover.

cards.stock: orthodontic treatment capacity measured in clinician chair-hours per corrected malocclusion
cards.evidence: Matched retrospective cohort in the peer-reviewed orthodontic literature: routine visit 9.9 minutes with aligners against 13.6 minutes with fixed appliances, 2.6 fewer visits and 86.2 minutes less total chair time per case; a second controlled series reports about 4 fewer visits, 5.5 months shorter treatment and 93.4 minutes less chair time [class 1, matched cohort on the host flow]. Contradicted at the same class: one randomised study reports significantly higher chairside time with aligners, and the 2024 systematic review in Evidence-Based Dentistry on mild-to-moderate crowding reports more appointments and similar treatment duration, both at low to very low certainty. FY2025 clear aligner volume 2.6 million cases, +4.7%, on revenue of USD 3.2bn of USD 4.0bn total (Q4 and FY2025 results, 4 Feb 2026).
cards.note: Gate pass: FY2025 cash from operations USD 593.2m, capex USD 102.4m, free cash flow USD 490.8m; 2.9m shares repurchased in 2025 at an average USD 162.09 for USD 465.9m with USD 831.2m remaining under the USD 1.0bn programme at 31 Dec 2025; share count 73.6m at Feb 2025 and falling, three-year dilution negative; no buyout pending, no going-concern statement. A 9 pre-deduction: the stock is named and the chair-hour is the Layer 0 healthcare unit, but the majority of case volume is elective adult alignment, so the stock is not clearly load-bearing; moat -1 on one fail among two testable tests. B 12: the per-case chair-time saving is quantified at class 1 but contradicted at class 1, and elective volume adds clinician-hours to the host system rather than removing them. C1 1: the enlarging mechanism is documented in the company's own releases, an added indication cleared 18 Dec 2023 and a consumer tier marketed at children, against a ceiling of orthodontic case starts. C2 4: revenue is cash-pay and outside the reimbursed system, so a rebalance toward essential capacity neither grows nor destroys it. D_exit 2: 2.4 billion single-use aligners manufactured to date with no standard-format recovery route disclosed; the three fabrication sites are light and redeployable. E 6 on the slack test: three regional manufacturing sites (Juarez, Ziyang, Wroclaw), about 1 million unique aligner parts per day, 295k trained doctors and no customer above 10%, against a single proprietary aligner material; node test not applicable.
cards.host_flow: clinician chair-minutes and office visits per completed orthodontic case; host stock healthcare capacity per clinician-hour; Layer 0 id healthcare

cards.stock: patients with severe aortic stenosis whose valve has not been replaced, and hospital bed-days consumed per aortic valve replacement
cards.evidence: PARTNER 3 (NEJM 2019, randomised, n=1,000 at 71 centres): mean index hospitalisation 2.9 days for TAVR vs 7.4 days for SAVR (median 3 vs 7, p<0.001), low-risk indication on the FDA label since Aug 2019; PARTNER 3 economic substudy (Circulation 2023, n=929 US patients): TAVR economically dominant vs SAVR at 2 years, ~95% probability of high value. EARLY TAVR (NEJM 28 Oct 2024, n=901): death, stroke or unplanned CV hospitalisation 26.8% vs 45.3% over median 3.8 years [class 1, randomised trial with a resource endpoint, on the regulator's label]
cards.note: Gate pass on the FY2025 numbers below. A base 18: untreated symptomatic severe aortic stenosis carries ~50% two-year mortality and 40% of severe AS patients remain untreated (ACC secular-trends report, 11 Jun 2024), so the stock is load-bearing and outside range; less 1 for the single moat fail. B 21 is the bottom of the top band, not the middle: the trial evidence is class 1 on a bed-day endpoint, but Edwards discloses no unit volume, so its share of the host flow rests on a third-party share estimate applied to the registry denominator. C1 5, not 6 to 7: the FDA approved the SAPIEN 3 platform for asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis on 1 May 2025, the first TAVR label in asymptomatic patients, which is the company widening the population it sells to and therefore its own ceiling; the disease itself is age-driven and not manufactured, so the band top rather than runaway. C2 6, not 7: revenue is a premium reimbursed device price, which under the recorded embedded-economics ruling cannot occupy the band reserved for revenue that survives a rebalance. D_exit 3: the implanted valve is handled at end of durability by valve-in-valve rather than explant (1,346 explants against 410,720 TAVRs, CMS 2012-2024), while delivery systems are single-use disposables. E 7: manufacturing in California, Utah, Singapore, Costa Rica and Ireland, no customer concentration, offset by hand-sewn bioprosthetic assembly that is slow to relocate. F_clock 5 on the higher of the two readings; the adoption numbers put it at the shoulder, not the steep phase.
cards.host_flow: hospital bed-days consumed per aortic valve replacement, and aortic valve replacements delivered per year; host stock healthcare (Layer 0 id: healthcare)
cards.attribution: ~63%, computed: US aortic valve replacements 119,293 in 2023 (100,501 TAVR, STS/ACC TVT Registry across 838 sites; 18,792 isolated SAVR, STS National Database); Edwards TAVR FY2025 sales $4.5bn with a third-party share estimate of ~75% of US TAVR (Life Science Intelligence, 2025) gives ~75,400 of 119,293. Edwards discloses no unit count itself
cards.ceiling: US aortic valve replacements performed per year: 119,293 in 2023 (100,501 TAVR, STS/ACC TVT Registry; 18,792 isolated SAVR, STS National Database), against 40% of severe aortic stenosis patients recorded as undertreated (ACC secular-trends report, 11 Jun 2024)
cards.penetration: ~63% of US aortic valve replacements, 2023
cards.enlarging: FDA approval of the SAPIEN 3 platform for asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis, 1 May 2025, the first TAVR label in asymptomatic patients, on EARLY TAVR: a company-obtained widening of the population the product is sold to

No. 2022-1877, en banc rehearing denied, cert. petition No. 24-428 filed 11 Oct 2024); price: pass (Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 releases state average selling prices were stable globally and attribute growth to procedure volume, so price is falling against US CPI); exit: silent (no exit fee, minimum-volume or exclusivity clause found; Medtronic, Abbott and Boston Scientific valves remain purchasable at the same hospitals). One fail among two testable tests: subtract 1
cards.clock_basis: adoption: ceiling 119,293 US aortic valve replacements (2023), penetration ~63%, doubling 6.4 years at FY2025 TAVR growth of 11.5% (shoulder, 4 to 5); asset basis reads 5 (substitution for surgical AVR on a reimbursement and guideline clock) and governs as the higher of the two
cards.gate_note: Pass. FY2025 sales $6.07bn, +11.5%; net cash from operating activities $1,595.2m, up $1,052.9m on 2024; cash ~$3.0bn against total debt ~$0.6bn at 31 Dec 2025; shares outstanding 586.9m at end-2025 after more than $800m repurchased during 2025 including a $500m accelerated repurchase announced 19 Aug 2025, so the three-year share count fell rather than diluted; no pending buyout; no going-concern language.
cards.verifier_reason: Attribution survives challenge: iData/Life Science Intelligence put Edwards at 72.3% of the US TAVR market in 2025, within 3 points of the card's 75%, so the ~63% share of 119,293 US aortic valve replacements (2023) stands and B 21 is earned on class 1 evidence (PARTNER 3, NEJM 2019, n=1,000, 2.9 vs 7.4 index bed-days). Moat tests confirmed: average selling prices stable globally (Q2 2026 release, 23 Jul 2026), Edwards v. Meril patent enforcement stands, one fail, A 17 correct. Gate confirmed: 580.8m shares at 31 Jan 2026 after more than $800m repurchased in 2025, no going-concern language. C1 corrected to 4: the card documents the enlarging mechanism the rubric names first, an indication the company widened (FDA approval of SAPIEN 3 in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis, 1 May 2025, on EARLY TAVR, NEJM 28 Oct 2024, n=901), and a second amplifier, re-intervention inside the company's own valve (1,346 explants against 410,720 TAVRs, CMS 2012-2024, end of durability handled by valve-in-valve); two documented amplifiers do not sit at the top of the 2-to-5 band. D_exit corrected to 2: explant rate 0.33%, the degenerated bioprosthesis stays in the patient with the second device placed inside it and coronary access constrained, and each procedure consumes a single-use delivery catheter. Two recording errors that do not move a band: clock_basis applies the company-wide 11.5% to TAVR, whose FY2025 sales of $4.5bn grew 8.6% constant currency (Q4 2025 release, 10 Feb 2026), so doubling is 8.4 years not 6.4, still the shoulder, and F_clock 5 stands on the asset basis; penetration is computed against procedures already performed, which is throughput, not the healthcare ceiling the table specifies (patients in the labelled indication), so the recorded 63% is the attribution restated. Total 76, tier unchanged.

cards.stock: operating-room and post-operative bed-day capacity consumed per operation, and the open-surgical trauma imposed on the patient
cards.evidence: Meta-analysis of randomised trials of robot-assisted abdominopelvic surgery (Surgical Endoscopy, 2024): length of stay ratio of means 0.695 (95% CI 0.615 to 0.774) robotic vs open, and weighted mean difference -0.73 days vs laparoscopic with significantly longer operative time; Annals of Surgery meta-analysis of 230 studies from 22 countries including 34 randomised trials across seven oncologic procedures: 1.9 days shorter stay vs open and 0.5 days vs laparoscopic [class 1, randomised trials, resource endpoint]. Against that, instruments and accessories revenue of $5.08bn in 2024 across 2,683,000 procedures is ~$1,894 of consumables per procedure, before the ~$1.60m system
cards.note: Gate pass on the balance-sheet facts below. A base 17: the stock is named and load-bearing (Lancet Commission on Global Surgery 2015: 5 billion people without access to safe affordable surgery and 143 million additional operations needed each year), less 3 for three moat fails. B 18 rather than the top band: the bed-day reduction is quantified in randomised trials against open surgery, but the same trials show significantly longer operative time, which consumes the operating-room half of the same stock, and the ~$1,894 per procedure of consumables runs the other way. C1 4: the unit is an installed base of proprietary consumables with programmed usage limits and third-party repair contractually barred, which is the amended text's own example of adjacent demand for the company's own products; 11,106 systems at 31 Dec 2025 and guidance of 13% to 15% procedure growth for 2026 on that base. C2 5: da Vinci is the premium option inside a fee-for-service system and the per-procedure consumable premium is what a rebalance toward cost per outcome squeezes; surgery itself survives. D_exit 2: EndoWrist instruments expire at a programmed use counter and cannot lawfully be reprocessed by third parties, and 870 of the 1,721 systems placed in 2025 were da Vinci 5 displacing X and Xi. E 6: systems built in Sunnyvale, Peachtree Corners and the Shanghai joint venture, instruments in Sunnyvale and Mexicali, Ion in Blacksburg and Shanghai, endoscopes in Germany, no customer concentration, but the 10-K discloses sole- and single-sourced components and the customer has no second source of instruments by design. F_clock 4: penetration 1.0% is below the 3% threshold, so the adoption override is unavailable and the name stays on the displacement clock.

cards.stock: sterile-procedure capacity: the share of invasive procedures and implanted single-use devices that reach the patient reliably sterile
cards.evidence: Mechanism-class evidence only: ethylene oxide sterilises more than 20 billion medical devices a year in the US, about 50% of all device types, with no viable alternative for many device geometries and materials (Rutala and Weber, Am J Infect Control 2023; FDA and AdvaMed); CDC estimates 518,000 healthcare-associated infections in US hospitals in 2023, about 1 in 38 inpatients on any given day, with surgical site infection rates showing little change. STERIS discloses no processed-unit or installed-base volume, so the study cannot be applied to its own throughput [class 3, independent system study, company volume not disclosed]
cards.note: Gate pass on the FY2026 numbers below. A base 18: the stock is the rubric's own worked example, load-bearing and outside range on the CDC 2023 count; less 1 because only one of the three moat tests was testable, so moat: unmeasured. B 14 is the step 3 cap, not a judgement of direction: the direction is correct and the mechanism class is documented by FDA, AdvaMed and CDC, but STERIS publishes revenue by segment (Healthcare $4,208.6m, AST $1,138.5m, Life Sciences $588.8m in FY2026) and no unit volume, so neither its share of the 20 billion US devices nor a per-cycle performance metric is available. C1 5: service revenue rose 11.1% and consumables 7.3% in FY2026 against total revenue of 9%, the company describing the shift as strengthening recurring revenue on its own installed base; no widened indication or consumer tier is documented, so the band top. C2 6: sterility demand grows with any rebalance toward infection prevention, but AST, 19% of FY2026 revenue, rides the single-use disposable device flow that a materials rebalance shrinks. D_rep 4 rather than 5: the sterilizers and consumables are replicated units, but the last five years of growth include Cantel Medical at $3.6bn in Jun 2021 and the BD surgical instrumentation acquisition, and AST is built facility by facility. D_exit 2: EtO plants are single-purpose sites carrying two-to-three-year compliance retrofits under the 2024 NESHAP (reconsideration proposed 12 Mar 2026) and gamma plants carry cobalt-60 source decommissioning. E 6: the slack test reads 8 on more than 60 owned or leased AST facilities across three regions with no customer above 10% of segment revenue, but the node test caps at 5 to 7 because no site's share of throughput is published, and the lower governs. F_now 3 rather than 4: the dated growth is revenue, not units, and the company names price as one of its three drivers.
cards.host_flow: invasive procedures and single-use devices delivered sterile per year, and healthcare-associated infections avoided per procedure; host stock healthcare (Layer 0 id: healthcare)
cards.attribution: not computable: STERIS discloses FY2026 revenue by segment (Healthcare $4,208.6m, AST $1,138.5m, Life Sciences $588.8m) but no device, cycle or installed-base volume, so its units cannot be divided by the 20 billion US ethylene-oxide-sterilised devices or by US procedures; B is held at the step 3 cap of 14
cards.ceiling: more than 20 billion medical devices sterilised with ethylene oxide in the US each year, about 50% of all device types (Am J Infect Control 2023; FDA, AdvaMed); on the healthcare side 518,000 US healthcare-associated infections in 2023 (CDC, released 2026)
cards.penetration: not computable: no processed-unit, cycle or installed-base volume disclosed (FY2026 10-K, year ended 31 Mar 2026)
cards.enlarging: installed base of dedicated consumables and service attached to STERIS capital equipment: FY2026 service revenue +11.1% and consumables +7.3% against total revenue +9%, described by the company as strengthening recurring revenue; no widened indication or consumer tier documented
cards.largest_node: none disclosed: the AST network is more than 60 owned or leased facilities across the Americas, Europe and Asia (FY2025 10-K) and no single site's share of throughput is published
cards.moat_tests: interface: silent (steam sterilizers accept third-party wrapped instrument sets and third-party biological and chemical indicators, while V-PRO and System 1E run dedicated STERIS chemistries; no third-party listing establishing the interface and no patent enforcement against a substitute in the last five years found, the only located patent action being the 2000 VHP matter); price: fail (FY2026 results state revenue growth of 8.7% was driven by higher volume, pricing and favorable foreign exchange across all segments, naming pricing as a growth driver); exit: silent (no exit fee, minimum-volume or exclusivity clause found; ISO 11135 and 11137 revalidation on moving a device to another sterilizer is a regulatory, not contractual, switching cost, and no FTC divestiture condition was located on the 2021 Cantel merger). Fewer than two tests testable: subtract 1, moat: unmeasured
cards.clock_basis: asset: penetration not computable, so the adoption override is unavailable; scored on hospital capital and consumable procurement cycles and on the EtO NESHAP compliance cycle, years
cards.gate_note: Pass. FY2026 (year ended 31 Mar 2026) revenue from continuing operations $5.94bn, +9% on $5.5bn, organic +8.7%; free cash flow $982.9m; gross debt to EBITDA ~1.2x and debt to total capital 21.3% at 31 Mar 2026; quarterly dividend raised to $0.63 and a $1bn repurchase authorisation in place, so the three-year share count is not diluted; no pending buyout; no going-concern language.
cards.verifier_reason: The interface test was misread as silent. STERIS's own 10-K defines consumable revenue as including dedicated consumables including V-PRO, SYSTEM 1 and 1E consumables, and VAPROX HC (59% hydrogen peroxide) is sold for the V-PRO maX, maX 2, s2, 1 Plus, 60 and 1 systems only; that is the filings describing proprietary consumables, which the amended test 1 makes a fail. With price already failed on the fiscal 2026 release naming price alongside volume, two of the two testable tests fail: subtract 3, not 1, so A is 15 on the base of 18. B corrected to 11: the card holds neither number the step 3 cap presupposes. Attribution is not computable (no device, cycle or installed-base volume in the FY2026 10-K, year ended 31 Mar 2026) and no per-unit performance metric is disclosed either, so the fallback the rule names is empty; the evidence is a mechanism-class count (more than 20 billion US devices sterilised with ethylene oxide a year, Am J Infect Control 2023) that cannot be applied to STERIS throughput, and the host-side number runs against the card: of the 518,000 US healthcare-associated infections in 2023, 61% were not associated with a device or procedure, and the rate fell from 1 in 31 inpatients in 2015 to 1 in 38 in 2023 (CDC 2023 point-prevalence survey, 13,653 patients at 218 hospitals). Direction is correct and asserted, which is the 8-to-14 band; 14 is the ceiling of that band, not the reading. Gate outcome confirmed but one figure is wrong: fiscal 2026 revenue from continuing operations rose 9% to $5.9bn with constant currency organic growth of 7%, not the 8.7% organic the gate note states; free cash flow $982.9m against $787.2m confirmed. Total 61, moving the card out of T4 into exit-review.

cards.stock: steel held in returnable, standard-format circulating units ,  the world fleet of ISO containers and road tank and trailer bodies, and the virgin steel drawn each year to replace them
cards.evidence: Direction correct, asserted only, mixed across segments, no host number. CIMC sold 2,224,900 TEU of standard dry containers in 2025 (-35.2%) and 208,200 TEU of reefers (+50.2%), with container manufacturing revenue of RMB 43.009bn (27.5% of group revenue), net profit RMB 1.882bn and a gross margin of 13.38%. The group publishes no virgin-versus-secondary steel input per TEU, no take-back or recovery volume, and no service-life or reuse figure for the boxes it sells; the modular-building line that is unambiguously a circulation loop (units described as made from recycled steel and recyclable at end of life, more than 200 projects delivered) is not a disclosed reportable segment with a volume. Against it, offshore engineering revenue was RMB 17.9bn (+8.35%) with net profit RMB 1.1bn (+371.79%), more than the whole group's attributable profit, and that yard's work includes FPSO hulls contracted through Seatrium for Petrobras's Atapu and Sepia presalt oil fields alongside six offshore wind turbine installation vessels [class 5, company assertion; no baseline, period or n for any flow endpoint]
cards.note: A 12 with no moat deduction. The stock is named and load-bearing ,  global goods movement runs on the standard box, and three Chinese manufacturers make more than 96% of the world's dry containers and effectively all reefers ,  but it is not outside its viable range: the fleet is in surplus, newbuild output fell to a decade low in 2025 and Drewry describes the equipment surplus as manageable and receding, and container prices fell to $1,752 per TEU in 2025 from $1,985 in 2024. The attachment is also diluted: container manufacturing is 27.5% of FY2025 revenue, energy, chemical and liquid food equipment (CIMC Enric) RMB 26.3bn (+6.3%), logistics services 17.7% of 2024 revenue, and the group also runs offshore engineering and a finance arm. B at the class-5 cap of 10 and at the mixed-segments band: no host-flow number with a baseline, period and n exists for the container business, and the offshore yard and the finance segment run against the direction of the rest. Rebound absorbed and recorded although B is below 15: the drain (new containers put on the market) fell, CIMC's own dry box volume by 35.2% and world newbuild output to a decade low, while the need series rose, global container port throughput from 876M TEU (2023) to 937.3M (2024) to 1.012bn TEU (2025, +8%). C1 6 at the bottom of neutral: demand tracks world container throughput and fleet replacement CIMC does not create, ceiling and penetration are recorded, and no enlarging mechanism is documented. C2 4 at the bottom of neutral: a rebalance toward longer service life and reuse of boxes reduces newbuild demand directly, which is what the 2025 collapse in dry-box volume is, and the offshore FPSO hull work and the finance segment need the present system, while CIMC Enric's marine clean-energy orders (above RMB 10bn cumulative) and the reefer line grow in a rebalance. D_rep 4: the container, the tank and the trailer are replicated standard units made in 11 dry-container production bases with 2 million TEU of annual capacity, 34 container plants and service bases in South, East and North China and 22 manufacturing bases and R&D centres across China and Europe, but the group also grows by enlargement into bespoke one-off hulls, airports, finance and logistics. D_inhib 4: operating cash flow of RMB 18.514bn, a dividend and two buyback programmes fund the group without fresh capital, but attributable net profit of RMB 221M on RMB 156.611bn of revenue is a 0.14% margin. D_exit 3: a steel box is scrapped into secondary steel and resold into storage and modular building, but the offshore yard is the part of this group that has stranded assets before, and one-off hull and rig work strands when an order is cancelled. E 5 on the slack test alone, the bottom of the neutral band: production is genuinely distributed across 34 plants and 22 bases and the product is modular and repairable, but no customer-concentration disclosure was located and effectively all dry-container capacity sits inside one country's export and tariff regime. Node test not applied, this is a product company. F_clock 3 on the asset basis: a container is a 15-year asset and the fleet it belongs to turns over on that cycle; the adoption override is unavailable because unit volume fell 35.2% in 2025. F_now 2: the dated momentum is in the smaller segments, not the corrected flow ,  the BOREAS installation vessel delivered 8 Jan 2025 and Norse Wind delivered on schedule to DEME on 15 Oct 2025 with six more under construction, offshore net profit +371.79%, reefers +50.2% ,  while dry containers, revenue and profit all fell. Jurisdiction: china-direct, penalty applied by the assembler, not here.
cards.host_flow: virgin steel tonnes put on the market as new containers per unit of container throughput carried, and tonnes of goods moved per box over its service life, measured at the shipping lines and lessors that operate the fleet; host stock: recoverable material stocks held in returnable form; Layer 0 id: materials
cards.attribution: computable at the unit level: CIMC sold 2,224,900 TEU of dry containers and 208,200 TEU of reefers in 2025 and is reported at roughly 45% of world container manufacturing, the largest single share of the three Chinese makers that account for more than 96% of world dry-container output; the group discloses no tonnage of steel consumed, no secondary-steel share and no reuse or take-back volume, so its share of the material flow itself is not computable
cards.ceiling: containers put on the market: world newbuild container production, which fell to a decade low in 2025 (CIMC dry-box volume 2,224,900 TEU, -35.2%), against a world fleet Drewry describes as carrying a receding equipment surplus. Need series: global container port throughput 876M TEU (2023), 937.3M TEU (2024), 1.012bn TEU (2025, +8%)
cards.penetration: about 45% of world container manufacturing output, 2025; 2,433,100 TEU sold (dry plus reefer) against 11 dry-container production bases holding 2 million TEU of annual capacity
cards.enlarging: none ,  no statement in the filings or in a regulator's finding that use of CIMC's containers raises the total number of containers put on the market or widens the population they are sold to
cards.largest_node: n/a ,  product company, the node test is not applied; the slack test governs alone
cards.moat_tests: interface: pass by definition (the product is the ISO 668 and ISO 1496 container, a standard rivals implement ,  the rubric's own named case ,  and CIMC's boxes are interchangeable across every carrier, lessor, crane and chassis in the world fleet); price: pass (the price per unit of the corrected flow fell to $1,752 per TEU in 2025 from $1,985 in 2024, -11.7% nominal against a Chinese consumer price index at or below zero over the same year, and the group attributes the fall to intensified market competition rather than naming pricing as a growth driver); exit: silent (no exit fee, minimum-volume or exclusivity clause located, and no regulator or court finding of a captive customer; buyers move between CIMC, Dong Fang and CXIC without documented switching cost, but no document establishes that either way). Two testable, no fails, no deduction
cards.clock_basis: asset: a container is a 15-year asset and the fleet it belongs to turns over on that cycle, so the correction lands on an infrastructure clock of decades; adoption basis unavailable, unit volume fell 35.2% in 2025 and no doubling time exists
